record.context_brief: Balanced excited random walks in dimensions two and higher
record.original_question: Consider a balanced excited random walk, meaning that for every site z, direction e, and visit number i one has ω(z,e,i) = ω(z,-e,i), so the local cookies do not create directional bias. Under uniform ellipticity and either i.i.d. or stationary-and-ergodic cookie environments, is every such walk recurrent in dimension 2 and transient in dimensions d >= 3?

evidence.quote: (IID)              the family (ω(z, ·, ·))z∈Zd of cookie stacks is i.i.d. under P.
(SE)                    the family (ω(z, ·, ·))z∈Zd is under P stationary and ergodic with respect to the shifts on Zd.
(UEL) There is κ > 0 such that for all z ∈ Zd , e ∈ E and i ∈ N : P-a.s. ω(z, e, i) ≥ κ.
More generally, consider measures P which are balanced in the sense that P-a.s. ω(z, e, i) = ω(z, −e, i) for all z ∈ Zd, e ∈ E, i ∈ N.
One may wonder, whether any balanced ERW satisfying (IID) (or (SE)) and (UEL) is recurrent if d = 2 and transient if d ≥ 3.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $d \ge 2$ and let $E = \{\pm e_1, \dots, \pm e_d\}$ denote the set of unit vectors in $\mathbb Z^d$. A cookie environment is a collection $\omega = (\omega(z, e, i))_{z \in \mathbb Z^d,\, e \in E,\, i \in \mathbb N}$ of nonnegative numbers with $\sum_{e \in E} \omega(z, e, i) = 1$ for every $z, i$, drawn from a probability measure $\mathbb P$. Given $\omega$, the excited (cookie) random walk $(X_n)_{n \ge 0}$ on $\mathbb Z^d$ starts at $X_0 = 0$ and, conditionally on its past, jumps from its current site $X_n = z$ to $z + e$ with probability $\omega(z, e, i)$, where $i$ is the number of previous visits of the walk to $z$ (including the current one).

Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item (Uniform ellipticity) There exists $\kappa > 0$ such that $\mathbb P$-almost surely, $\omega(z, e, i) \ge \kappa$ for all $z \in \mathbb Z^d$, $e \in E$, $i \in \mathbb N$.
\item Either (IID) the cookie stacks $(\omega(z, \cdot, \cdot))_{z \in \mathbb Z^d}$ are i.i.d.\ under $\mathbb P$, or (SE) this family is stationary and ergodic with respect to the lattice shifts.
\item (Balanced) $\mathbb P$-almost surely, $\omega(z, e, i) = \omega(z, -e, i)$ for all $z, e, i$.
\end{itemize}

Prove or disprove: under these hypotheses, the walk $(X_n)$ is recurrent (i.e., returns to $0$ infinitely often a.s.) when $d = 2$, and transient (i.e., $|X_n| \to \infty$ a.s.) when $d \ge 3$.
artifact.status_search_result: The recurrence/transience question for balanced excited random walks is a well-known open problem. In two dimensions, partial progress has been made: Peres, Schapira and Sousi (Annals of Probability, 2023, arXiv:2110.15889) proved a 0-1 law for the set of recurrent sites and obtained range bounds, but the full recurrence conjecture in d=2 remains open. The transience claim in d ≥ 3 is also still open in this generality. Surveys (e.g., Menshikov–Popov–Wade-style overviews and the Springer chapter "An Overview of the Balanced Excited Random Walk") list these as open conjectures.

status_evidence.title: Balanced Excited Random Walk in Two Dimensions
status_evidence.snippet: We prove that the set of recurrent sites is either everything or nothing, and give nontrivial bounds on the range.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress in d=2 (0-1 law for recurrent sites) but full recurrence in 2D remains open.

status_evidence.title: An Overview of the Balanced Excited Random Walk
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of balanced excited random walks including open problems on recurrence and transience.
status_evidence.claim: Recurrence in 2D and transience in d≥3 are listed as open conjectures.

status_evidence.title: A balanced excited random walker returns home
status_evidence.snippet: The conjecture is that in two dimensions the balanced excited random walk is always recurrent.
